newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African rightist convicted of assaulting blacks.
newsitem.headline: S.African rightist convicted of assaulting blacks.

text.p: Defiant white rightist leader Eugene Terre'Blanche was convicted by a South African court on Wednesday of trying to murder a black employee and assaulting another black man.
"Today the war has started," the Afrikaner Resistance Movement (AWB) leader told reporters outside the courtroom in Potchefstroom west of Johannesburg after walking out on the magistrate's judgment.
Terre'Blanche was found guilty of attempting to murder former employee Paul Motshabi, 27, who suffered severe brain damage after a heavy beating in March last year.
He was also convicted of serious assault on another black man, named as John Thembeni Ndzima, last November.
"The accused is found guilty on both charges," magistrate Chris Eksteen ruled.

Immediately after the magistrate spoke, Terre'Blanche jumped from his seat in the dock and told Eksteen: "May God watch over you for what you have said. It will echo in the homes of every Boer (Afrikaner)".
Fighting back tears, Terre'Blanche added: "You have become the accomplice of the (ruling) African National Congress... You are a traitor...the judgment is a political judgment."
As his followers, jammed into the packed courtroom, broke into applause and cheered "Hear, hear", Terre'Blanche walked out of the court.
The magistrate did not attempt to stop the right-wing leader, but said as he left the court that he wanted to put on record that the outburst had prevented him from reading out his whole judgment.
Another right-wing leader, the Boerestaat Party's Robert van Tonder, threatened that Afrikaners would take unspecified actions if the magistrate imprisoned Terre'Blanche.
"There will be serious trouble if the man is jailed," Van Tonder told reporters outside the court building.
